ghats.name: Basara Godavari River Bathing Ghat
ghats.description: Sacred bathing steps along Godavari River where pilgrims take holy purification dips (Nadi Snanam) before main temple entry and Aksharabhyasam rituals.

significance: The Godavari River at Basara is considered spiritually cleansing, with holy dips believed to erase karmic burdens. The river serves as the core site for the historic Godavari Pushkaralu festival.

mega_events.significance: Widely known as the 'Kumbh Mela of South India'. While traditionally celebrating Jupiter's transit into Simha Rasi (Leo), the upcoming 2027 cycle marks an essential multi-state pilgrimage milestone.
mega_events.verified_crowd_data: 1.5 to 2 million total footfall over 12 days; daily counts reach 150,000 to 200,000 on opening (Aadhi Pushkaram) and closing (Anthya Pushkaralu) days.
mega_events.safety_measures: District Collector deploys emergency medical camps, strict river-barricading zones, and automated crowd-tracking technology.

festive_surges.river_activity: Joint temple-and-river festival. Mandatory purification holy bath (Nadi Snanam) before main temple entry and pradakshinas.
festive_surges.verified_crowd_data: 15,000 to 20,000 pilgrims crowd the bathing ghat steps from pre-dawn (2:30 AM) until noon.

festive_surges.river_activity: Floating lamp ritual (Deepotsavam / Deepa Danam) along the banks; devotees launch lit clay lamps (diyas) onto river water.
festive_surges.verified_crowd_data: 5,000 to 10,000 onlookers gather around 5:30 PM to 7:00 PM aligning with evening Harathi.

daily_traditions.operational_details: Held at Godavari River Aarti Point. Peaceful, no ticket fee, recommended photography and cultural spot.
Performed at designated sub-section of the ghat for ash immersion similar to Kashi.
Parents bring young toddlers for foot splashing or a quick dip before going to the temple.

monsoon.advisory: If heavy floods occur, step access to the bathing ghat may be temporarily closed by the district administration for safety.

safety_rules: Because crowd densities peak to dangerous levels during Pushkaralu, emergency medical camps, strict river-barricading zones, and automated crowd-tracking technology are deployed by District Collector. Step access to bathing ghat may be temporarily closed during heavy monsoon floods for safety.
